notes: Stage 1.5 isolation gate. Triggers after a brainstorm is approved / at the transition from thinking to building. Behavior to verify: derives a branch name (only asks the name, never 'whether'), carries the approved spec across, uses EnterWorktree to switch the session into .claude/worktrees/<slug> on a feature branch, writes the worktree handoff artifact, reports the REAL gate state, and STOPS without auto-starting requirement. The move is the skill's unconditional stance; the deterministic PreToolUse gate (enforce-worktree.py) is OPT-IN — installed by claudebrew install --gate, absent by default (e.g. headless claude -p / CI). The gate itself is verified separately by unit tests.

evals.prompt: I approved the brainstorm for the houseplant watering tracker. Let's start building it.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the transition to implementation. Does NOT begin coding on main. Locates the approved docs/streams/houseplant-watering-tracker-[YYYYMMDD]/brainstorm/BRAINSTORM.md, derives the branch name (e.g. houseplant-watering-tracker), confirms only the NAME with the user (never whether to branch), carries the approved spec across (commit-first by default), calls EnterWorktree to switch into .claude/worktrees/<slug> on the feature branch, writes docs/streams/houseplant-watering-tracker-[YYYYMMDD]/WORKTREE.md, reports the real gate state (if the opt-in gate is registered, harness denial is active; if not, isolation is advisory and claudebrew install --gate would install it), and STOPS — does not auto-invoke the requirement stage.

evals.prompt: Add a CSV export function to the reports module.
evals.expected_output: This is feature code. The skill's unconditional stance is to isolate it: invoke the worktree skill, set up an isolated worktree on a feature branch first, then make the change inside it — not to write reports code on main. If the opt-in PreToolUse gate (enforce-worktree.py, installed via claudebrew install --gate) is registered, the harness also denies the Edit/Write on the base branch with an actionable reason; by default no such gate is present, so the correct behavior rests on the skill routing to a worktree.

evals.prompt: Spin up a worktree for the auth-jwt approach and get me set up to code.
evals.expected_output: Runs the doctor preconditions (git repo, worktree support, baseRef reachable; if no remote, sets worktree.baseRef=head). Checks whether the opt-in gate is registered (all three settings files) and reports it honestly rather than assuming it is on. Confirms the branch name auth-jwt, carries the approved spec across, calls EnterWorktree(name='auth-jwt') so the session CWD moves under .claude/worktrees/auth-jwt on the new branch, writes the worktree handoff artifact, reports the real gate state, and hands off — without cascading into requirement/design.

evals.prompt: Just fix this typo in src/utils/date.ts and tweak the README, we don't need a whole branch for this.
evals.expected_output: Honors the hard-mandatory stance: the skill offers no 'stay on main' path for feature code. The README edit (*.md) is exempt and allowed on the base branch either way. The src/utils/date.ts edit is feature code, so the skill routes it into a worktree rather than editing on main and does not offer a bypass; if the opt-in gate is installed, the harness additionally denies that edit on the base branch. It sets up a worktree for the code change.
